assets.prompt: Generate one photographic editorial illustration for a Korean agency article explaining how to simplify website inquiry forms. Wide exact16:9, target1600x900. Overhead authentic editorial still life on a warm off-white designer desk: two physical paper stacks, left cluttered oversized stack of numerous blank form strips with many gray lines, right three neat pale-blue cards with simple hand-drawn icons for person, contact envelope, message bubble. A real person's hand moves an unnecessary paper strip aside. Mechanical pencil, one blue binder clip, natural window sunlight, tactile paper fibers, subtle deep-indigo accents. Sophisticated magazine photography, not a 3D clay render, not a glossy browser mockup. Physical conceptual scene only, no screen UI and no claim of actual client workspace. NO readable text, NO letters, NO numbers, NO logos, NO charts, NO personal information. Crisp but calm composition, enough negative space, clear visual comparison of too many fields versus only necessary fields. Only this final image.

Create one flat editorial information graphic for a website inquiry-form article. Exact wide16:9 target1600x900. Contemporary Swiss editorial vector-like visual, crisp simple shapes, NO 3D, NO photorealism. Light icy-blue background, charcoal-indigo and vivid cobalt linework with small coral and mint accents. Show an intuitive left-to-right process with four large clearly separated outlined symbols: a form sheet with three short lines, a secure server cabinet, an envelope arriving in a tray, then a speech bubble containing a check. Connect with flowing arrows. Between server and envelope a separate small coral dashed branch goes down to an alert triangle and loops back toward the form, clearly illustrating an error and retry route, with no misleading success path. Large generous spacing, rounded cards with thin borders, minimal grid texture, accessible strong contrast. NO text, NO letters, NO numbers, NO logos, NO UI screenshot, NO analytics. Conceptual explanatory infographic only. It must look distinctly different from magazine photography and 3D thumbnails. Only final image.
